title: Circling the House
hookLine: seven circuits anticlockwise around the Ka'ba

lines: A PLAIN HOUSE IN BLACK CLOTH.
cards: After miles of here I am, the pilgrims arrive. They come through the gates of the mosque in Mecca, and there it is: a plain stone building draped in black cloth, standing in the middle of a wide open floor.
The Qur'an, in surah twenty-two, names what pilgrims do at this House, and Pickthall's translation puts it in a few words: "go around the ancient House." Not enter it. Not climb it.
Go around it. Today, the walk that goes in circles on purpose.

teach.b: First, the shape. Tawaf means going around. The pilgrim circles the Ka'ba with it on the left, so the whole crowd turns the same way, counterclockwise, like one slow wheel.
You met the House itself back on day forty-two. Second, the count. Jabir ibn Abdullah gave a long account of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ's pilgrimage, kept in Sahih Muslim.
When the Prophet reached the House, Jabir says, he went around it, moving briskly for three circuits and walking for four. Seven in all. The brisk pace for the first three has a name: ramal.
Third, what kind of act it is. A report in Tirmidhi has the Prophet saying that going around the House is like prayer, except that in it you may speak, so whoever speaks should speak only good.
A prayer you can walk, and even talk in, as long as the talk is good. People recite, make their own requests, repeat words of praise, or walk in silence.
Fourth, the center. Every circle needs one point that doesn't move. Crowds from everywhere, in plain cloth, all turning around the same still house.

In Islam the Ka'ba is not the one worshipped; it's the House, and the worship is for God alone. But the walk teaches with the body something that's hard to teach with words. Everything in the crowd is moving.
The center isn't. Each circuit brings the pilgrim back to the corner where it began, and the next one starts again from there.

how: Pilgrims perform tawaf by walking seven circuits around the Ka'ba counterclockwise, starting and ending at the corner of the black stone, often reciting Qur'an or making du'a; men walk briskly in the first three circuits of the arrival tawaf.

o: going around the Ka'ba seven times, with it on your left
bowing toward the Ka'ba from anywhere in the world
a long walk back and forth between two hills

games.q: circling the House — tap the pairs.
p: the brisk pace of the first three

s: the walk around the Ka'ba is worship of the Ka'ba
the Ka'ba is the House they walk around; the worship is for God.
the Prophet moved briskly for three circuits and walked for four
so Jabir reports in Sahih Muslim.
a report in Tirmidhi says you may speak, as long as you speak good.

games.q: you reach the Ka'ba after the long journey. what does the Qur'an tell pilgrims to do at the House?
o: stand at the door and wait.
games.why: "go around the ancient House" (22:29). the act is a circle, around a center that stays still.

practice: Walk seven slow laps of a room or a yard, always in the same direction, counting on your fingers if it helps; this isn't tawaf, just a way to feel its shape in the body.
If you pray, say words of praise you know as you go; if not, keep your attention on your steps. When the seven are done, stand still and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Tawaf. Going around the Ka'ba, seven times, with the House on the left. Today's word.

orig.note: going around: the circling of the Ka'ba.

carryVoice: Your line: around the center. Everything else can turn while the center holds. See you tomorrow.
